content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High auth-failure rate detected for auth-proxy-prod. ~3.5k failed token refresh attempts from a small set of CIDRs; possible leaked tokens or credential spray. Pager: @oncall. Runbook: security/credentials-exposure-v2.

Janet S.: I'm on it. Oncall who? what's the immediate customer impact? :eyes:

Ryan M.: I'm oncall for auth today — taking it. quick glance: spike concentrated on /v1/token/refresh; many 401->429 retry patterns. UA: 'curl/7.82.0' and consistent X-Forwarded-For ranges 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/25.

Shanice K.: If tokens were leaked, priority is service-account rotation + stop-any-more-exfil. I'll own key rotation. Suggest: (1) block offending CIDRs at WAF/LB, (2) rotate telemetry-indexer svc token, (3) restrict S3 bucket exposure.

Leo P.: Pushing WAF ACL now to block 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/25 on LB-1234. ETA ~2m. Also preparing temporary rate-limit rule on auth-proxy.

Janet S.: Copy. Ryan, can you confirm whether any customer identifiers were present in the logs that were forwarded externally? we may need to prepare customer-notify.

Ryan M.: Quick grep of forwarded logs shows debug-forwarder sent records with "session_id" and partial email hashes to s3://staging-logs-bucket during 2026-03-17T01:12Z -> 2026-03-17T13:05Z. That looks like an exposure window. Recommend removing public access to that bucket immediately and mark for forensics (do not delete).

Shanice K.: Agreed. Immediate steps (I'll coord):
1) Edge: block CIDRs (Leo)
2) Rotate telemetry-indexer SVC token (IAM) and revoke old token
3) Revoke any affected API keys that show refresh activity > 50/day
4) Remove public read on s3://staging-logs-bucket and enable bucket-level logging + retention hold
5) Prepare customer notification draft after Legal signs off

Command I'll run for s3 lock (doing now):
```bash
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket staging-logs-bucket --policy '{"Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:GetObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::staging-logs-bucket/*"}]}'
```

emma (legal): Please preserve all objects and metadata for the exposure window. Do not purge. We need timeline, affected customers, and any downstream recipients before sending notifications. Also preserve backend keys and host logs for PID.

ops-bot: WAF rule applied to LB-1234 blocking 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/25 — rollout completed 10s ago.

Leo P.: Telemetry-indexer token rotation initiated. New token written to vault at secret/telemetry/indexer/prod (access: sec-eng+ops). Old token will be revoked in 120s. I'll follow up with rotation PR URL once done.

Janet S.: Confirmed: public read removed from staging-logs-bucket and bucket ACL set to private. Ryan — can you run query to find customer accounts with >100 refresh attempts from those CIDRs during window? we need a preliminary affected list for Legal/CS.

Ryan M.: Running query now, will drop CSV to the private incident folder. Preliminary: 18 distinct customer accounts showing anomalous refresh activity; no evidence of active session takeover or customer outages detected. This looks like credential scraping rather than live hijack.

incident-bot: Incident severity escalated to P1 (credentials exposure). Notify: SecEng, Customer Success ops, and Exec watch. Playbook: security/credentials-exposure-v2 (link).

Shanice K.: I'll draft the customer-facing note (short, factual: what we saw, mitigation, recommended rotate keys) and post for Legal review. Also scheduling a follow-up to lock down debug-forwarder verbosity and retention policy.

Janet S.: Handoff: Ryan remains on incident for next 60 minutes to finish affected-customer list. Security (Shanice) will lead remediation. Legal (emma) will approve customer-notify. I'll update incident channel with timeline and next steps. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
